page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 9 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across compute and memory operations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a Passmark CPU score of 65,056.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,030.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 222.1 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 95.0 GB/sec for large block write operations. In LLM inference tests, the server achieves 353.0 tokens/sec for text generation with a small 135M model, though performance drops to an average-tier 3.46 tokens/sec when executing a large 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i-flex.12xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that require high CPU performance without the massive memory footprints of memory-optimized instances. The lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which represents a tradeoff for I/O-heavy applications. This instance is well-suited for compute-intensive tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
